title: Add Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) support
description:
Add optional MFA/2FA for enhanced account security.

Requirements:
- TOTP-based MFA (Time-based One-Time Password)
- Use speakeasy or otplib library

- MFA recovery flow (if user loses device)
- Settings page to enable/disable MFA
- Rate limiting on MFA verification attempts

Recommended library: speakeasy (https://www.npmjs.com/package/speakeasy)

title: Add process management (PM2 or systemd)
description:
Current issue: Services crash and accumulate zombie processes
Current state: Using tsx watch + serve via nohup, no auto-restart

Problems:
- Zombie processes accumulate over time
- No automatic restart on crash
- Manual cleanup required (pkill -9)
- No log rotation

Solution: Use PM2 or systemd for process management

PM2 benefits:
- Auto-restart on crash
- Log rotation built-in
- Process monitoring
- Easy deployment (pm2 deploy)
- Simple commands (pm2 restart, pm2 logs)

Systemd benefits:
- Native to the system
- Starts on boot automatically
- Journal integration
- More stable/permanent

Recommendation: PM2 for ease of use, systemd for production stability

Acceptance criteria:
- Services auto-restart on crash
- No zombie process accumulation
- Logs rotated automatically
- Start on system boot
close_reason:
✅ Completed - systemd process management deployed to production

Successfully installed and configured systemd services for both frontend and backend.

What was deployed:
- venn-backend.service - API server with auto-restart and logging
- venn-frontend.service - Static file server
- Both services enabled to start on boot
- Integrated with journalctl for log management

Results:
- ✅ Services running stable (10+ min uptime tested)
- ✅ No zombie processes
- ✅ Auto-restart on crash configured (Restart=always, RestartSec=10)
- ✅ Start on boot enabled
- ✅ Production site working: https://venn-demo.avan.academy

Benefits achieved:
- Auto-restart on crash
- Automatic zombie process reaping
- Start on system boot
- Integrated logging via journalctl
- Production-grade process management
- Security hardening (NoNewPrivileges, PrivateTmp)

Documentation:
- deployment/SYSTEMD_EXPLAINED.md - comprehensive guide
- deployment/README.md - quick reference
- Services installed to /etc/systemd/system/

Commands for daily ops:
- sudo systemctl status venn-backend
- sudo systemctl restart venn-backend
- sudo journalctl -u venn-backend -f

title: Switch to private IPs and restrict public port access
description:
Security hardening: Use private IPs for inter-service communication

Current state:
- Frontend talks to backend via public IP
- Backend ports exposed publicly (8000, 9000)

Required changes:

1. Backend/Frontend Communication:
   - Use private IPs for localhost communication
   - nginx → backend: localhost:8000 (already correct)
   - Keep public access only through nginx (443/80)

2. Firewall Rules:
   - Block all ports above 8999 from public internet
   - Allow: 80, 443 (nginx), 29689 (SSH)
   - Block: 8000 (backend), 9000 (serve)
   - Keep localhost communication unrestricted

3. Implementation:
   - Configure ufw or iptables firewall
   - Update deployment docs
   - Test that services work through nginx
   - Verify direct port access blocked

Benefits:
- Backend not directly accessible from internet
- Reduced attack surface
- Force all traffic through nginx (better logging/security)

Environment: Both dev and prod machines have private IPs

References:
- ufw docs: https://help.ubuntu.com/community/UFW
- iptables guide for service isolation
close_reason:
✅ Completed - Switched to internal IP for server communication

Network security improvements implemented:

**What changed:**

title: Fix SPA routing (404 on /contacts refresh)
description:
Issue: Refreshing on /contacts or other routes returned 404
Cause: serve was not configured for SPA routing
Fix: Added --single flag to serve command

serve --single tells the static server to always return index.html,
letting React Router handle client-side routing instead of looking
for physical files.

Updated:
- justfile: Added restart-frontend command with --single
- OPS.md: Documented SPA routing issue and solution
- Production: Frontend restarted with --single flag

Status: Fixed and deployed

Commit: e37f74d

title: Migrate DNS to Cloudflare
description:
Future improvement: Migrate from Duck DNS to Cloudflare DNS

Why Cloudflare:
- Better performance (global CDN)
- Free tier includes DDoS protection
- Better API for automation
- Can handle both dynamic DNS (via API) and static DNS
- Domain registration built-in (optional)
- Analytics and monitoring

Migration scenarios:

1. Dynamic DNS (changing IP):
   - Use Cloudflare API to update A records
   - Script: curl to Cloudflare API on IP change
   - Benefit: Same dynamic DNS capability, better features

2. Fixed DNS with Cloudflare-registered domain:
   - Transfer/register domain with Cloudflare
   - Point A record to server IP
   - Enable proxying for DDoS protection
   - Benefit: Full production setup

Implementation:
- Set up Cloudflare account
- Add domain (or use existing)
- Configure A record for server IP
- Update OAuth callback URLs
- Test SSL certificate renewal
- Update deployment docs

Don't prioritize until:
- Duck DNS proves limiting, OR
- Ready to move to production-grade setup, OR
- Want to learn Cloudflare API/features

References:
- Cloudflare API docs: https://developers.cloudflare.com/api/
- Dynamic DNS guide: https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/manage-dns-records/how-to/managing-dynamic-ip-addresses/
close_reason:
✅ Completed - Already using Cloudflare DNS

The venn-demo.avan.academy domain is already fully on Cloudflare.

**Current setup verified:**
- ✅ avan.academy domain uses Cloudflare nameservers (cody/katja.ns.cloudflare.com)
- ✅ venn-demo.avan.academy proxied through Cloudflare CDN (172.67.159.136, 104.21.33.69)
- ✅ Cloudflare Origin Certificates in use
- ✅ Cloudflare DDoS protection active
- ✅ Cloudflare proxy enabled (orange cloud)

**Benefits we're already getting:**
- Global CDN for faster content delivery
- DDoS protection
- Free SSL certificates
- Analytics and monitoring
- Automatic HTTPS rewrites

**No migration needed** - we went straight to Cloudflare when setting up venn-demo.avan.academy. Never used Duck DNS for this project.

This issue was created as a future improvement when we thought we were on Duck DNS, but the production deployment used Cloudflare from day one.

Issue can be closed as complete (nothing to migrate - already there).
